decisions_for_captain.title: Does the RT1062 get its own I2C path to the ADC6120, or does the S3 configure it over K1BR?
decisions_for_captain.recommendation: ESCALATED WITHOUT A RECOMMENDATION - the audio lane raised it as 'a decision, not a chore' and refused to resolve it.
decisions_for_captain.evidence: Measured: U6-RTC is on NEITHER I2C_SDA NOR I2C_SCL. The RT1062 has no I2C access anywhere on this board. The bus is four slaves (INA226, ADC6120, ST25R3916B, LIS2DH12) and ONE master socket - the ESP32-S3. The RT1062 does own the ADC6120's data and clock pins; it does NOT own and cannot reach its control port - sample rate, channel configuration, PDM mode, PLL setup, gain and the GPIO1/GPI1/GPI2 function assignments all live behind I2C. So every audio experiment on this validation board requires the ESP32-S3 to be alive and to configure the ADC on the RT1062's behalf, with the request crossing K1BR - on a board whose stated purpose includes resolving a 113 dB versus 123 dB converter question. Either a deliberate split (S3 = configuration master, RT = data master) that the ownership matrix must be updated to state, or an oversight. Separately, contracts/motion-interface.md names the RT1062 as default owner and the RT1062 has no data path to the sensor at all. Isolation IS achievable - select the master leg, not the sensor leg - but there is no RT master leg to select until two RT1062 balls are assigned.

decisions_for_captain.title: The Type-C source requirement: 2.40 A at 5 V needs a source advertising 3.0 A, nothing measures CC, and the largest load cannot be shed.
decisions_for_captain.recommendation: (a) SENSE AND THROTTLE - bring J1 CC1/CC2 to 5.1 kOhm Rd AND tap both to RT1062 ADC inputs through protection dividers, and put U4-PWR2.1 on an RT1062 GPIO. Costs two ADC channels, one GPIO and four passives; fits the board's stated validation mission; and it is the only option that keeps the 2.40 A design point honest rather than aspirational.
decisions_for_captain.evidence: The board needs 12.0 W. USB Type-C R2.0 Table 4-18 gives three advertisements at 5 V: Default USB (500 mA, 2.5 W - 20% of requirement), 1.5 A (7.5 W - 62%), 3.0 A (15 W - the only one that covers it, 80% utilised). Three consequences, none addressed: (1) the board cannot read the advertisement - J1 has NO Rd at all so it never attaches, and J7's correct 5.1 kOhm Rds go straight to GND with no ADC tap, so nothing distinguishes a 15 W charger from a 2.5 W laptop port; (2) the board cannot shed its largest load - U4-PWR2.1 is hard-tied to 5V_SYS, so 51% of the peak is unconditionally enabled before firmware runs; (3) advertisement detection wants to live on J1, which is the connector with no CC circuit at all. Option (b) 'design to 1.5 A' does NOT survive the arithmetic: after the 1.030 A non-LED coincident peak the LED ceiling falls to roughly 0.15 A, which is not a lighting product - unless someone proves the Wi-Fi/BLE TX burst and the NFC TX burst cannot overlap, which is a firmware-scheduling claim, not a hardware one. And the trunk window carries only 2.4% of total slack (3.000/2.397 = 1.252 against the part's own 1.222 tolerance span), so exactly one standard ILIM value fits and any growth in the LED ceiling leaves NO SOLUTION AT ALL from a 3 A source. Option (c) 'specify the supply' is zero added circuitry and the weakest position for a validation board that will be plugged into whatever is on the bench.

decisions_for_captain.title: Single-ended versus differential NFC antenna topology.
decisions_for_captain.recommendation: RATIFY SINGLE-ENDED WITH CABLE (AN5592 S2.3) - which is what the board already is. Needs a decision-register entry and a contract line.
decisions_for_captain.evidence_for: The K1 antenna is external and remote on a U.FL coaxial lead, and AN5592 S2.3 is ST's topology for exactly that; ST support directs a STEVAL-ST25R3916B user with a coaxial external antenna straight to AN5592 and confirms it applies to the ST25R3916B. Differential over a coaxial lead is not a case AN5592 documents. AAT is unavailable either way (S2.4: not possible with a cable, because any change in cable parameters detunes the reader), so ratifying costs nothing K1 has. The EXT_LM removal S2.2 requires is already satisfied - K1 has no EXT_LM circuit and no AAT varactors, so pins 17, 18 and 19 already meet the single-ended requirements. Fewer components, less area.
decisions_for_captain.evidence_against: READ RANGE. DS13541 S4.2.1: single-driver mode halves the LC tank component count and cost 'but also the output power is reduced.' AN5592 S2.2: a single-ended signal is unbalanced and 'more prone to noise and interference' - on a board carrying a switching buck, LED drivers and USB. AN5276 S2 recommends the differential design for low-power applications 'because gives the best range.' Part of the receive path is given up: the peak detector reads RFI1 only at gain 0.7, the AM demodulator mixer uses both inputs at 0.55, and the amplitude and phase detectors are differential between RFI1 and RFI2. AN5592 S2.3 admits only a limited set of target matching impedances (for example 4, 8, 16 Ohm), so less design freedom - AND it requires a SECOND MATCHING NETWORK AT THE ANTENNA END, tuned to the cable's characteristic impedance, which is a product part that does not exist and is in no BOM.
decisions_for_captain.if_differential: NFC-D4 becomes a real wiring defect again, and RFO2, RFI2, a second CVDR1/CVDR2 pair, a second EMC inductor and a second Cs/Cp arm must all be added. Larger than the single-ended repair, and not the topology AN5592 documents for a coaxial lead.
decisions_for_captain.either_way: IO configuration register 1 bit single = 1 with rfo2 = 0 is required for the as-built board, because the device default is differential. That belongs in the contract regardless of the ruling.

decisions_for_captain.title: Which rail does the TPS3808 supervisor monitor - 3V3 with the fitted G33, or 1V15_CORE with a part change to the adjustable G01 plus a divider?
decisions_for_captain.recommendation: Monitoring 3V3 with the fixed-threshold G33 is the defensible reading of D13.1.
decisions_for_captain.evidence: The repair cannot dodge this. Even wired to 3V3 (as its sibling U7-RTC is), U16 reports on the shared 3V3 rail, not on anything RT-specific. The RT1062 core rail is 1V15_CORE, produced by the RT1062's own internal DCDC through L4-RTC. Monitoring the core needs a PART CHANGE, not a wire edit. RT_PWR_VALID is decorative at BOTH ends today - SENSE floats and no consumer is attached.

decisions_for_captain.title: PDM route-A series value: keep 0 Ohm, or move to 22 Ohm to current-limit a double-populate?
decisions_for_captain.recommendation: 22 Ohm - harmless at 3.072 MHz into a MEMS mic clock input, and already the house value elsewhere on this board.
decisions_for_captain.evidence: A real interlock would need a mux or a physically shared single footprint, which is a bigger change than this validation board warrants.

decisions_for_captain.title: MIC_PWR_EN safe default: rail ON at power-up (as built), or OFF until firmware asks?
decisions_for_captain.recommendation: Not recommended by the lane - but IF THE DEFAULT STAYS ON, rename the net MIC_PWR_EN_N so firmware cannot get the sense wrong.
decisions_for_captain.evidence: The name inverts the behaviour: writing 1 to 'MIC power enable' turns the microphone off. The current default is DEFINED, not indeterminate - but it was probably not CHOSEN. If the intended safe default is 'microphone unpowered until firmware asks for it', R9 must pull UP to 3V3_MIC_REG - Q1's source, not the main 3V3 rail, so Vgs can never be reversed during rail sequencing.

decisions_for_captain.title: F1-PWR1: re-rate the trunk bead, or remove series filtering from the trunk entirely?
decisions_for_captain.evidence: Two independent problems wanting different fixes. Position: a ferrite in series with the whole rail, upstream of the eFuse and followed by C1-PWR1 22 uF, forms an LC tank across the hot-plug event, and the overshoot lands on the eFuse input whose OVLO is 5.46 V. Input EMI filtering generally does not belong in series with the full trunk ahead of the protection device.

decisions_for_captain.recommendation: The conventional match to a 10 kOhm-at-25 C NTC is 10 kOhm, but the value should put the NTC mid-span across the intended monitoring range - that choice belongs to the thermal lane (D15).
decisions_for_captain.evidence: The audit asserts only that the resistor must exist. Its absence is what makes both channels unreadable.

decisions_for_captain.recommendation: A. Add B on top only if a firmware-commanded LED blackout is wanted for thermal or fault response - which, given the branch-protection gap, is a conversation worth having, but a separate one.
decisions_for_captain.evidence: B does not remove the need for A's resistors, it adds to them - a Hi-Z buffer still leaves the strip data line undefined. A costs no RT1062 pads and no firmware sequencing; B costs two RT pads.

disagreements.question: Which field does EasyEDA actually order from, for R1-PWR1 and R8-PWR2?

lane_a.position: 'both are ordered and fitted as 10 kOhm' - the COMPONENT library reference and the bound device both name RC0402FR-0710KL.1, and the correct LCSC code sits in Supplier Part, 'the field EasyEDA does not use for ordering'

lane_b.position: 'the field that carries the orderable identity is Supplier Part', so R8 orders as a genuine 3.48 kOhm and the LED limit is a determined 0.96 A

disagreements.resolution: GENUINELY OPEN, and it changes the SEVERITY of RQ-046/RQ-047. RQ-056 (export the BOM and read it) settles this and nothing else does. The repair is identical either way, so this does not block execution - only the urgency.

disagreements.question: Did U3-PWR2.5 regress between the two DRC runs?

lane_a.position: 'one pin went the wrong way - U3-PWR2.5 became floating between the two runs', handed to A2-RAILS as a regression

lane_b.position: it was never connected - the BUCK_PG wire has been off-sheet since it was drawn, and the 12:17 DRC ran BEFORE the PG pull-up transaction executed at ~04:56Z

disagreements.resolution: Effectively resolved in favour of lane B - the 12:17 log predates the transaction, so its silence is not evidence of a working connection. Recorded because the DRC single-network warning is NOT a reliable dangling-net detector: MOTION_INT_S3 was a one-pin net in the frozen source and appeared in neither run's list. Its silence is not evidence.

VDD_USB_CAP (U6-RTC.K8) decoupling value: NXP publishes NO capacitance value in IMXRT1060CEC Rev 4 Table 82 or HDG Rev 3 Table 2 - notable because the adjacent VDD_HIGH_CAP is specified at 0.22 uF + 4.7 uF. Only the general rule applies (ripple below 5% Vp-p). Recorded as TUNE_TBD rather than passed silently.
